follow-up time: Until assessment of cerebral palsy and/or developmental delay
exposure: presence of a known sentinel event
birth in the era before the implementation of neonatal hypothermic therapy
cohort: 248 infants born after 34 weeks of gestation with cord arterial pH <7 or base excess ≤-12 mmol/L at birth
finding: Infants born with umbilical artery pH <7 have a high chance of survival (89.5%), but a cord arterial pH of <6.9 and an Apgar score at 5 minutes <7 are independent risk factors for death or adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was not found to be significantly associated with adverse outcomes in infants born with umbilical artery pH <7.
